title: Telemetry-aware function-schema validator and resumable-invoke adapter for SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: SDK users across Python, TypeScript, and Go are integrating function/tool calling. We see two recurring pain points: (1) silent schema mismatches that lead to hard-to-debug failures downstream, and (2) poor streaming ergonomics when an invocation fails mid-stream (no easy resume/checkpoint semantics). Goal: implement a lightweight, cross-SDK validator that enforces function schemas with configurable strictness and emits structured telemetry, plus a resumable-invoke adapter that provides checkpointed stream delivery with safe retry semantics. The work focuses on library ergonomics, observable failures, and deterministic retry behavior so application authors can instrument and recover from partial invocations without heavy rework.
acceptance_criteria: Validator API available in Python/TS/Go with same semantics and feature parity
Three validation modes supported: strict (error on extra/missing fields), coercive (attempt to coerce types), and tolerant (warn-only)
Telemetry emitted for each invocation: schema_validation_result, validation_errors_count, preinvoke_latency_ms, token_latency_sample, retry_reason, resume_checkpoint_id
Resumable-invoke adapter exposes simple resume(checkpoint_id) primitive and preserves idempotency for side-effectful tools via idempotency_key header
End-to-end example added to SDK docs: sample webhook-enrichment and streaming long-output resume flow
Unit + integration tests added covering schema mismatch, type coercion edge cases, mid-stream failure and resume, and telemetry events (mocked)
implementation_notes: Design a small canonical schema-walk utility (no heavy deps) to validate JSON payloads against function param definitions and annotate errors with path and severity
Expose validator options: mode, max_error_report=5, auto_coerce_types=true/false, allow_unknown_fields boolean
Telemetry: use existing SDK telemetry channel; provide clear event names and attributes to Console (schema.validation, invoke.attempt, invoke.resume) and include sample token_latency percentiles

Resumable-invoke adapter: checkpointing will rely on per-invocation KV checkpoint IDs stored client-side; server returns a checkpoint token on stream partial success; resume flow must replay missing user input and pass checkpoint token
Retries: differentiate transient network vs schema fatal errors. Do not auto-retry on strict-schema failures. For coercive mode, retry with coerced payload once and emit distinct telemetry event
Backwards compatibility: keep existing simple invoke() as-is; new helpers available under sdk.invoke.resumable and sdk.validate.functionSchema namespaces
Cross-language: align surface area rather than identical method signatures—provide idiomatic bindings in each language while matching telemetry field names
testing_plan: Unit tests for validator: missing required field, extra fields, type mismatch, nested array/object edge cases
Integration test: simulate mid-stream SIGPIPE/network drop and assert resume returns consistent final output and emits resume checkpoint telemetry
Load test: validate telemetry payload size/throughput for high-frequency invocations; ensure no P95 telemetry latency > 100ms impact
Compatibility test: run sample TS and Python examples against local mock runtime that returns checkpoint tokens
Security: verify idempotency_key is optional but recommended for side-effectful tool calls; document best practices
